items.answer: Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.
Presence is the psychological side that captures whether a user perceives the immersive qualities that are generated.

An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real: when a person experiences an environment through sensory organs and fails to distinguish that environment from the person's real environment, perceiving it as the real environment, the technology producing that experience is an immersive technology.
